title: The State Is Enough
dek: A Markov process is a bet: that you can choose a description of "now" so complete that the past adds nothing. This is what that bet buys — matrices you can raise to a power, stationary distributions, mixing times — and where computer science has cashed it: PageRank, MCMC, Viterbi, Kalman, MDPs and reinforcement learning, branch predictors, cache models, queueing and capacity planning, and the state-size fight between attention and state-space models. It closes with where the bet loses.
byline: 28 September 2026 · Every number in a figure is computed from the model printed beside it
description: What a Markov process is, what the memoryless property buys you, and where computer science uses it: PageRank, MCMC, HMMs, MDPs, branch predictors, queueing, and modern sequence models.
og_description: The Markov property is a modelling bet, not a fact about the world: choose a state so complete that history adds nothing. This explainer works through the arithmetic — transition matrices, stationary distributions, spectral gaps, generators — and then through the places computer science cashes it: PageRank and random walks, Metropolis-Hastings and Gibbs, Viterbi and Kalman, MDPs and RL, two-bit branch predictors, Markov prefetchers, M/M/1 queues and capacity planning, diffusion models, and the KV-cache-versus-recurrent-state argument in sequence architectures.
twitter_description: Markov processes, taken apart: the memoryless bet, the arithmetic it buys, and fourteen places computer science cashes it — from PageRank to branch predictors to the state-size fight between attention and SSMs.
